### <a name="crowdsec--appsec"></a>`crowdsec::appsec`

Acts as a collector for AppSec hub items: declares
`crowdsec::appsec::config` and `crowdsec::appsec::rule` resources for
the supplied lists and orders them before the appsec.yaml acquisition
file. The service must see referenced items in the hub before it
starts, otherwise it fails with "unknown data source appsec".

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `crowdsec::appsec` class:

* [`listen_addr`](#-crowdsec--appsec--listen_addr)
* [`appsec_configs`](#-crowdsec--appsec--appsec_configs)
* [`appsec_rules`](#-crowdsec--appsec--appsec_rules)

##### <a name="-crowdsec--appsec--listen_addr"></a>`listen_addr`

Data type: `String`

Address and port used by the AppSec listener.

Default value: `'127.0.0.1:7422'`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--appsec--appsec_configs"></a>`appsec_configs`

Data type: `Array[String]`

List of AppSec config names (`appsec-configs` hub items) to install.

Default value: `['crowdsecurity/appsec-default']`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--appsec--appsec_rules"></a>`appsec_rules`

Data type: `Array[String]`

List of AppSec rule names (`appsec-rules` hub items) to install.

Default value: `[]`

### <a name="crowdsec--bouncer--openresty"></a>`crowdsec::bouncer::openresty`

This class manages the bouncer component configuration and can optionally
manage an OpenResty/nginx http-context Lua hook snippet. The hook is opt-in
so deployments with complex existing Lua can merge the generated directives
in their own OpenResty profile instead of loading another Lua block.

### <a name="crowdsec--lapi"></a>`crowdsec::lapi`

Two modes:

* **Remote LAPI** — both `login` and `password` are supplied (e.g. pinned
  from Hiera/Vault). The credentials file is rendered from the template
  so the local watcher authenticates against an external LAPI.

* **Local LAPI** (default) — `login`/`password` are unset. The credentials
  file is left untouched so the auto-generated values from the crowdsec
  package postinst keep working. To recover from a previous run that
  wiped the file (or a database that was reset out of band), Puppet
  re-registers the local watcher whenever the login in the credentials
  file is missing from `cscli machines list`.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `crowdsec::lapi` class:

* [`url`](#-crowdsec--lapi--url)
* [`login`](#-crowdsec--lapi--login)
* [`password`](#-crowdsec--lapi--password)
* [`manage_server_listen_uri`](#-crowdsec--lapi--manage_server_listen_uri)
* [`server_listen_uri`](#-crowdsec--lapi--server_listen_uri)
* [`cscli_path`](#-crowdsec--lapi--cscli_path)

##### <a name="-crowdsec--lapi--url"></a>`url`

Data type: `String`

URL used by local clients to reach the CrowdSec Local API.

Default value: `'http://127.0.0.1:8080'`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--lapi--login"></a>`login`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional login/machine name for LAPI authentication.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--lapi--password"></a>`password`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional password for LAPI authentication.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--lapi--manage_server_listen_uri"></a>`manage_server_listen_uri`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to manage api.server.listen_uri in /etc/crowdsec/config.yaml.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--lapi--server_listen_uri"></a>`server_listen_uri`

Data type: `String`

Address and port where the local API listens for machines and bouncers.

Default value: `'127.0.0.1:8080'`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--lapi--cscli_path"></a>`cscli_path`

Data type: `String`

Path to the cscli binary (provided via Hiera).

Default value: `'/usr/bin/cscli'`

### <a name="crowdsec--repo"></a>`crowdsec::repo`

Supports Debian/Ubuntu (APT) and RedHat/CentOS/Rocky/AlmaLinux (YUM/DNF).
All repository parameters are provided via module Hiera data
(data/Debian.yaml, data/RedHat.yaml) so adding a new distribution only
requires a new data file — no manifest changes needed.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `crowdsec::repo` class:

* [`apt_location`](#-crowdsec--repo--apt_location)
* [`apt_release`](#-crowdsec--repo--apt_release)
* [`apt_repos`](#-crowdsec--repo--apt_repos)
* [`apt_key_name`](#-crowdsec--repo--apt_key_name)
* [`apt_key_source`](#-crowdsec--repo--apt_key_source)
* [`apt_legacy_sources`](#-crowdsec--repo--apt_legacy_sources)
* [`yum_baseurl`](#-crowdsec--repo--yum_baseurl)
* [`yum_gpgkey`](#-crowdsec--repo--yum_gpgkey)
* [`yum_gpgcheck`](#-crowdsec--repo--yum_gpgcheck)

##### <a name="-crowdsec--repo--apt_location"></a>`apt_location`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

APT repository URL.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--repo--apt_release"></a>`apt_release`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

APT release (e.g. 'any' for packagecloud.io).

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--repo--apt_repos"></a>`apt_repos`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

APT component (e.g. 'main').

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--repo--apt_key_name"></a>`apt_key_name`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Filename for the APT signing key in /etc/apt/keyrings/.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--repo--apt_key_source"></a>`apt_key_source`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

URL to download the APT signing key from.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--repo--apt_legacy_sources"></a>`apt_legacy_sources`

Data type: `Array[String]`

List of stale .list files to remove before apt-get update runs.
Used to eliminate conflicts from the packagecloud.io bootstrap script.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--repo--yum_baseurl"></a>`yum_baseurl`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

YUM/DNF repository base URL. The string $basearch is
a YUM macro expanded at runtime, not a Puppet variable.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--repo--yum_gpgkey"></a>`yum_gpgkey`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

URL to the GPG key used for RPM signature verification.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--repo--yum_gpgcheck"></a>`yum_gpgcheck`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to verify RPM signatures (default: true).

Default value: `true`

### <a name="crowdsec--machine"></a>`crowdsec::machine`

Mirrors `crowdsec::bouncer::api_key` but for machines: remote log-processor
nodes authenticate to LAPI with a login/password pair rather than an API
key. Registering the machine here lets remote nodes connect with the same
credentials managed via Hiera (preferably hiera-eyaml).

Note: the password is only consumed on first registration. Rotating the
password here will not re-register an existing machine; remove it via
`cscli machines delete <name>` on LAPI to force re-registration.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `crowdsec::machine` defined type:

* [`password`](#-crowdsec--machine--password)
* [`machine_name`](#-crowdsec--machine--machine_name)
* [`cscli_path`](#-crowdsec--machine--cscli_path)

##### <a name="-crowdsec--machine--password"></a>`password`

Data type: `String`

Password the remote machine will use to authenticate.

##### <a name="-crowdsec--machine--machine_name"></a>`machine_name`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\z/]`

Machine name registered in CrowdSec; defaults to the resource title.

Default value: `$title`

##### <a name="-crowdsec--machine--cscli_path"></a>`cscli_path`

Data type: `String`

Path to the cscli binary (provided via Hiera).

Default value: `'/usr/bin/cscli'`
